what: How much of a whole-document answer retrieval can show the model
why: The /manage gap report on a real install listed sixteen unanswered questions. Eleven were one shape: enumerate a list, name the characters, summarise a document. They route to retrieval correctly and fail after it. This measures the ceiling - no model is called, because a model cannot list what it was never shown.

corpus.source: evals/golden-ftr/documents - US Federal Travel Regulation, public domain
corpus.note: Deliberately not written here. An enumeration corpus I wrote myself would be one where I had unconsciously kept the answer inside the budget.

the_number.question: what terms does the glossary define

the_finding: Raising k does not fix this. k=50 is eight times the shipped budget and more than half the entire corpus, and still reaches only 89%. BM25 ranks by term overlap and the query shares no vocabulary with the terms it is asking to enumerate. A whole-document question needs the document assembled, not ranked.

control.question: what transportation methods are authorized
control.floor: Unrelated queries still score 1-2 of 4, because 'common carrier' and 'privately owned' are ordinary phrasing in a travel regulation. The control's signal is 4/4 against that floor, not against zero.

sabotages: Shown all 92 chunks the glossary case reaches exactly 82/82 and 22/22 - the one that makes the 32% believable rather than a broken substring check.
Unrelated queries drop the control from 4/4 to 1-2/4, so it is not passing on ambient vocabulary.
Breaking the term extractor's word limit fails both the reference-list test and the shown-everything test.
not_measured: Whether the model, shown 26 of 82 terms, lists 26 or invents 82. That needs a model and belongs in a generation set. Only the ceiling is established here.

also_found.already_fixed: Four of the sixteen field questions were fixed on 2026-08-29 in 17818b9 and c56ada2 and are answered free today. They still appear because the gap query only clears a row when the question is asked again, and nobody re-asks a question that failed.
also_found.answered_wrongly: 'what does this document cover' was caught by the corpus tier and answered with an inventory of the whole collection - the only silent wrong answer among the sixteen, delivered grounded and ungated from the first branch of the cascade. Collateral from 17818b9, which put 'cover'/'covers' into the no-subject vocabulary so that 'what are the macro-categories of info they covers' would be recognised. Fixed here.
also_found.panel_copy: The report told the reader that 'answered in part' means the document is missing a section. For these eleven questions the section is not missing - it was in chunk seven. Both surfaces now name both causes.
